findings.title: Migration crashes when the embed_category site setting row is missing or matches no category
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. The `embed_category` setting defaulted to an empty string and is only persisted in `site_settings` if an admin actually changed it, so on most installs (and any fresh DB) the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking the upgrade. It also crashes if the setting was set to a value that doesn't match a category name exactly. The same pattern at line 15 crashes if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Both lookups need nil-safe handling before indexing into the result.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted verbatim and will never match lookups
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting supported entries with scheme and path (e.g. `http://discourse.org`, `https://example.com/1234`) — the removed specs in site_setting_spec.rb and embed_controller_spec.rb prove these worked, because the old code compared against `URI(h).host`. The migration inserts the raw setting values into the new table, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` looks up `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, so any migrated row containing a scheme or path will never match a referer. After upgrading, previously working embedded comments silently stop working for those sites. The migration should normalize hosts the same way the model's `before_validation` does (strip scheme and path) or insert via the model.

findings.title: embed_category is deleted even when no host rows were created
findings.body: If a site used feed polling with `embed_category` set but had no `embeddable_hosts` configured (feed-only embedding, which previously worked because `TopicEmbed.import` used the global `SiteSetting.embed_category`), this migration creates zero `embeddable_hosts` rows and still deletes the `embed_category` setting. From then on `TopicEmbed.import` uses `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which finds nothing, so imported topics fall back to the uncategorized category — or fail validation entirely when `allow_uncategorized_topics` is false and the embedding user isn't staff. The previously configured category assignment is lost with no replacement.

findings.title: Host values are interpolated into SQL without escaping
findings.body: The INSERT interpolates the setting value directly: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A value containing a single quote (legacy/malformed data in the old free-text setting) will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize`/`quote` or a parameterized insert.

findings.title: Migration is not reversible despite using `change`
findings.body: The migration uses `def change` but contains raw `execute` statements (data copy and `DELETE FROM site_settings`). Rolling back will raise ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration, and even a manual reverse can't restore the deleted `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` setting rows. This should be split into `up`/`down` with an explicit, safe down (or acknowledge irreversibility).

findings.title: No foreign key or cleanup for category_id
findings.body: `category_id` is `null: false` but has no foreign key, and the `EmbeddableHost` model has no `belongs_to` presence validation or dependent handling. Deleting a category leaves dangling `embeddable_hosts.category_id` values; `TopicEmbed.import` will then create topics pointing at a nonexistent category (PostCreator is given the stale id, and `ensure_topic_has_a_category` won't fix it since the id isn't nil), and the admin UI renders a missing category badge. Add a FK and/or handle category deletion.

findings.title: show always renders JSON, so direct navigation/refresh to /admin/customize/embedding breaks
findings.body: `show` unconditionally calls `render_serialized(...)`, which renders JSON for every format. The sibling customize pages (permalinks, colors, emojis, site texts) respond with an HTML page that boots the Ember admin app for non-XHR requests; this controller (and its missing view template) does not. Opening or refreshing `https://site/admin/customize/embedding` directly in a browser returns a raw JSON payload instead of the admin UI. Add `respond_to`/`format.html` handling plus the blank HTML view like the other admin customize controllers.

findings.title: update/destroy 500 on unknown id instead of 404
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking the result. For a stale or invalid id (e.g. two admins, one deletes a host while the other's page still shows it), `save_host(nil)` calls `nil.host = ...` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, both raising NoMethodError → 500. Additionally `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without verifying the wrapper param exists, so any request missing the `embeddable_host` key also 500s. Raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record doesn't exist and guard the params.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is nil (e.g. an API call to POST /admin/embeddable_hosts without a host value), this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `self.host = self.host.to_s` or skip the substitutions when host is blank.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host
findings.body: Neither the model nor the migration enforces uniqueness of `host`. The admin UI lets the same host be added multiple times with different categories, and `record_for_host` uses `.first`, so which category an embedded topic lands in becomes nondeterministic. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and a unique index (the migration's data copy should also dedupe).

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match; input host not downcased for comparison
findings.body: The format validation explicitly allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but keeps the port, so an admin can save `example.com:3000`. But `record_for_host` compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` — `uri.host` never includes the port — so that row can never match any referer and the site silently can never embed. Also the bound value isn't downcased, so a mixed-case referer host won't match `lower(host)`. Either reject/normalize ports on save or include the port (and downcase the input) in the lookup.

findings.title: Host validation regex rejects legitimate TLDs longer than 5 characters
findings.body: The regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` for the final label, so valid domains like `example.technology`, `example.international` or `example.museum` fail validation and can't be added as embedding hosts. The old free-text setting imposed no such restriction, so this is a new, undocumented limitation.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents were swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) that were deleted from the category file. The suite still passes only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory regardless of name, but the filenames are now actively misleading and the contents should be swapped back.

findings.title: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims
findings.body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer consults embeddable hosts at all. The spec still asserts that it "is false if embeddable_host is blank", but it passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false — it would pass identically if a host existed, so it guards nothing about the removed condition. The example should be renamed/rewritten to reflect the new contract (or removed).

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no request specs
findings.body: The specs for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) only assert the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. All the actual behavior added in this PR — creating/updating a host, the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` when category is blank, validation errors, unknown-id handling, destroy, and the embedding show payload — is completely untested, which is how the nil-record and nil-param crashes slip through.
